result.topic_en: Euler computes the reduced efflux velocity-height of water under assumed friction coefficients α, showing that smaller friction brings it closer to the frictionless value of 4⅓ feet, and proposes measuring the outflow experimentally to determine the true value of α.
result.transcription:
352 TENTAMEN THEORIAE

erit $\frac{\alpha b}{g}=\frac{1}{20}$ et $e^{\frac{\alpha b}{g}}-1=0,05127$ : atque $\frac{g}{\alpha}-l=50$.
Vnde fit:
$v=\frac{1}{3}+2,563=2,896$ pedum.
Hoc ergo casu altitudo celeritati, qua aqua effluit, debita tantum est $2,896$ pedum, cum frictione sublata ea futura esset $=4\frac{1}{3}$ pedum.

65. Si effectus frictionis minor esset, quam assumsi, celeritas aquae etiam magis accederet ad altitudinem $4\frac{1}{3}$ pedum. Quod quo clarius appareat, ponamus $\alpha=\frac{1}{6000}$, erit $\frac{\alpha b}{g}=\frac{1}{30}$, et $e^{\frac{\alpha b}{g}}-1=0,03389[?]$, atque $\frac{g}{\alpha}-l=90$, vnde fiet:
$v=\frac{1}{3}+3,05046=3,38379$ ped.
Altitudo ergo celeritati debita iam foret $3,38379$, ideoque propius ad $4\frac{1}{3}$ ped. accederet.

66. Vase autem huiusmodi constructo, per experimentum explorari potest, quanta aquae copia certo tempore effluet. Ponamus enim minuto primo effluere copiam aquae, quae sit $m$ ped. cub. atque pariter in pedibus erit $v=100000\,mm$, qui valor comparetur cum iis, quos pro $v$ ex hypothesibus $\alpha=\frac{1}{4000}$ et $\alpha=\frac{1}{6000}$ determinauimus, vel si hae hypotheses minus congruant, aliae calculo euoluantur, sicque innotescet verus valor ipsius $\alpha$. Expediet autem plura huiusmodi institui experimenta, antequam de vero ipsius $\alpha$ valore plane certi esse queamus.

CASVS

items.quote: Si effectus frictionis minor esset, quam assumsi, celeritas aquae etiam magis accederet ad altitudinem $4\frac{1}{3}$ pedum.
items.english: If the effect of friction were smaller than I assumed, the velocity of the water would approach even more closely the height of 4⅓ feet.

items.quote: Vase autem huiusmodi constructo, per experimentum explorari potest, quanta aquae copia certo tempore effluet.
items.english: Once a vessel of this kind has been built, it can be determined by experiment how much water flows out in a given time.

items.quote: vel si hae hypotheses minus congruant, aliae calculo euoluantur, sicque innotescet verus valor ipsius $\alpha$.
items.english: or if these hypotheses agree poorly, others should be worked out by calculation, and thus the true value of α will become known.

items.quote: Expediet autem plura huiusmodi institui experimenta, antequam de vero ipsius $\alpha$ valore plane certi esse queamus.
items.english: It will be advisable, however, to carry out several such experiments before we can be fully certain of the true value of α.
